root_cause.text: The page allocator does not clear the `page->private` field of a page when it is freed, allowing stale values to persist and propagate to tail pages when high-order pages are subsequently allocated and split.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided code shows the page freeing path in `free_pages_check` (lines 337-361) and the allocation path in `prep_new_page` (lines 474-505). In `free_pages_check`, there is no clearing of `page->private`. In `prep_new_page`, `set_page_private(page, 0)` is only called on the head page (line 501) and not on any of the tail pages of a high-order allocation. This allows stale `page->private` values to persist on tail pages, which can propagate when high-order pages are split.
